en: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Umawi narrated to us; they said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to us; both of them from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith: 'The best of this Ummah is the generation in which I was sent, then those who succeed them.' He added in the hadith of Abu 'Awanah: He said: 'And Allah knows best whether he mentioned the third or not,' like the hadith of Zahdam from 'Imran. And he added in the hadith of Hisham from Qatadah: 'and they swear oaths when they are not asked to swear oaths.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr al-'Abdi narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission. And in their hadith he said: 'I do not know whether he mentioned after his generation two generations or three.' And in the hadith of Shababah he said: 'I heard Zahdam ibn Mudarrib—and he came to me on horseback for a need—and he narrated to me that he heard 'Imran ibn Husayn.' And in the hadith of Yahya and Shababah: 'they make vows and do not fulfill them,' while in the hadith of Bahz: 'they fulfill them,' as Ibn Ja'far said.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar all narrated to us from Ghundar; Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu Jamrah: Zahdam ibn Mudarrib narrated to me: I heard 'Imran ibn Husayn narrating that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, the best of you is my generation, then those who succeed them, then those who succeed them, then those who succeed them.' 'Imran said: 'I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said after his generation twice or thrice: "Then after them there will be a people who will bear witness without being asked to testify, who will be treacherous and not be trusted, who will make vows and not fulfill them, and obesity will appear among them."'

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah; (H) and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us; both of them from Abu Bishr, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that in the hadith of Shu'bah: Abu Hurayrah said: 'So I do not know whether twice or thrice.'

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr; (H) and Isma'il ibn Salim narrated to me: Hushaym informed us: Abu Bishr informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best of my Ummah is the generation in which I was sent, then those who succeed them.' And Allah knows best whether he mentioned the third or not. He said: 'Then a people will succeed who love plumpness, bearing witness before they are asked to testify.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to me: Azhar ibn Sa'd al-Samman narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Ibrahim, from 'Abidah, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The best of the people are my generation, then those who succeed them, then those who succeed them.' I do not know whether it was in the third or fourth that he said: 'Then there will remain after them a later generation whose testimony precedes their oath, and their oath precedes their testimony.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; both of them from Mansur, with the chain of transmission of Abu al-Ahwas and Jarir, with the meaning of their hadith, and in their hadith there is no mention of 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked.'

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abidah, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked: 'Which of the people are best?' He said: 'My generation, then those who succeed them, then those who succeed them. Then there will come a people whose testimony will outpace their oath, and their oath will outpace their testimony.' Ibrahim said: 'They used to forbid us, when we were young boys, from making covenants and testimonies.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us; they said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from 'Abidah al-Salmani, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best of my Ummah is the generation following me, then those who succeed them, then those who succeed them. Then there will come a people whose testimony precedes their oath, and their oath precedes their testimony.' Hannad did not mention 'the generation' in his hadith, and Qutaybah said: 'Then there will come peoples.'

Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri stated that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'A time will come upon the people when an expedition will be dispatched from among them, and they will say: "Look! Do you find among you anyone from among the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" And a man will be found, and victory will be granted to them through him. Then a second expedition will be dispatched, and they will say: "Is there among them anyone who saw the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" And victory will be granted to them through him. Then a third expedition will be dispatched, and it will be said: "Look! Do you see among them anyone who saw someone who saw the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" Then there will be a fourth expedition, and it will be said: "Look! Do you see among them anyone who saw someone who saw anyone who saw the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" And a man will be found, and victory will be granted to them through him.'

Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's; they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us: 'Amr heard Jabir reporting from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'A time will come upon the people when a group of people will go out on a military campaign, and it will be said to them: "Is there among you anyone who saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" They will say: "Yes," and victory will be granted to them. Then a group of people will go out on a military campaign, and it will be said to them: "Is there among you anyone who saw someone who accompanied the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" They will say: "Yes," and victory will be granted to them. Then a group of people will go out on a military campaign, and it will be said to them: "Is there among you anyone who saw someone who accompanied someone who accompanied the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" They will say: "Yes," and victory will be granted to them.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Aban all narrated to us from Husayn; Abu Bakr said: Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Mujammi' ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said: We prayed Maghrib with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and then we said: 'If only we sat until we prayed 'Isha' with him.' He said: So we sat, and he came out to us and said: 'Are you still here?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we prayed Maghrib with you, and then we said we would sit until we pray 'Isha' with you.' He said: 'You did well,' or 'You were right.' He said: Then he raised his head to the sky—and he would frequently raise his head to the sky—and said: 'The stars are a source of security for the sky; when the stars depart, there will come to the sky what it is promised. And I am a source of security for my Companions; when I depart, there will come to my Companions what they are promised. And my Companions are a source of security for my Ummah; when my Companions depart, there will come to my Ummah what they are promised.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is no alliance-making (hilf) in Islam, and whatever alliance existed in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance (Jahiliyyah), Islam only increases it in strength.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; they said: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) established an alliance (brotherhood pact) between Quraysh and the Ansar in his house in Medina.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to me: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: 'Asim al-Ahwal narrated to us; he said: It was said to Anas ibn Malik: 'Has it reached you that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no alliance-making in Islam"?' Anas said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) indeed established an alliance between Quraysh and the Ansar in his house.'

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) established brotherhood between Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and Abu Talhah.

Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi narrated to me: Khalid—meaning Ibn Makhlad—narrated to us: Sulayman—who is Ibn Bilal—narrated to me: Suhayl narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), exactly the like of this hadith of Ma'mar.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me; Ibn Rafi' said: 'narrated to us', and 'Abd said: 'informed us' 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah; (H) and Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best women who have ridden camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most affectionate toward a child in his youth and the most protective over a husband regarding what his hands possess.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me; 'Abd said: 'informed us' and Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) proposed marriage to Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, but she said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have grown old and I have dependents.' Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best women who have ridden [camels]...' then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yunus, except that he said: 'the most affectionate toward a child in his youth.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'The women of Quraysh are the best women who have ridden camels: the most affectionate toward a child and the most protective over a husband regarding what his hands possess.' He said: Abu Hurayrah would say right after that: 'And Mary daughter of 'Imran never rode a camel at all.'

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); and Ibn Tawus, from his father, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that he said: 'the most protective over a child in his youth,' and he did not say 'an orphan.'

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah; and from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best women who have ridden camels—one of the two narrators said: the righteous women of Quraysh, and the other said: the women of Quraysh—are the most affectionate toward an orphan in his childhood and the most protective over a husband regarding what his hands possess.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You will find among the worst of people the two-faced person who comes to these with one face and to those with another face.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Irak ibn Malik, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Indeed, the worst of people is the two-faced person who comes to these with one face and to those with another face.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; he said: I read to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, among the worst of people is the two-faced person who comes to these with one face and to those with another face.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah; (H) and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You will find people are like ores/minerals...' like the hadith of al-Zuhri, except that in the hadith of Abu Zur'ah and al-A'raj: 'You will find among the best of people in this matter [of leadership] those who have the greatest dislike for it until they fall into it.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You will find people are like ores/minerals: the best of them in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance are the best of them in Islam when they attain deep understanding of the religion. And you will find among the best of people in this matter [of authority] those who have the greatest dislike for it before they fall into it. And you will find among the worst of people the two-faced person who comes to these with one face and to those with another face.'

Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi narrated to us: Maslamah ibn 'Alqamah al-Mazini, the imam of the mosque of Dawud, narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'There are three traits I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning Banu Tamim, because of which I will never cease to love them thereafter.' And he related the hadith with this meaning, except that he said: 'They are the fiercest of people in fighting in the great epic battles,' and he did not mention the Dajjal.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'I will never cease to love Banu Tamim after three things I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say about them.' Then he mentioned the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Harith, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: 'I will never cease to love Banu Tamim because of three things I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "They are the sternest of my Ummah against the Dajjal." And when their charity (zakat) arrived, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "This is the charity of our people." And there was a female captive from among them in the care of 'A'ishah, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Emancipate her, for she is from the offspring of Isma'il (Ishmael)."'
